subject: Customer-controlled keys and operator demarcation for private deployment
messages:
From: Susan Park <susan.park@medicahealth.com>

Subject: Cust-key & operator access for private deploy

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo earlier this week — the private deploy flow looks promising. As we move to procurement I need a clear write-up on how Redwood expects to handle customer-controlled keys, operator access, and cross-border data movement for our VPC/on-prem option. Specifically: 

- Can Redwood staff ever decrypt customer data or prompts with BYOK?
- If you have an escrow/escape-hatch for keys, what are the conditions and approvals required?
- What telemetry and logs do operators see if they need to troubleshoot?
- Are there subprocessors outside the US that would touch metadata or logs?

We also need a sample DPA clause we can drop into our legal intake and a high-level timeline for procurement-signed infra changes.

For scope: attaching an Excel with our expected PII categories. Procurement will be on copy (procurement@medicahealth.com).

Best,
Susan
Head of InfoSec, MedicaHealth

Attachments: Medica_PII_Scope.xlsx (spreadsheet listing data categories)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cust-key & operator access for private deploy

Hi Susan — thanks for the clear list. High level answers first, then a short plan and an attachment with our playbook.

1) Customer-controlled keys (BYOK): If you elect BYOK, keys are provisioned by your KMS/HSM; Redwood never has access to the plaintext keys. We support HSM-managed keys (Cloud KMS/HSM or on-prem HSM) and an alpha flow for hardware keystores behind a customer gateway. Under BYOK, runtime encryption keys derived for the session are never exported in plaintext.

2) Escrow / break-glass: We can offer a keystore-escrow arrangement on a case-by-case basis. Escrow keys are stored encrypted and released only under a documented, multi-party approval flow (customer ops approval + legal signoff + Redwood security approval). We can sketch clause language; see attached playbook (redwood-private-deploy-keystore-playbook_v1.docx).

3) Operator access & telemetry: Operators may need to see diagnostic metadata (request IDs, timestamps, truncated token counts, error stacks). We will not surface unencrypted prompt or response text when BYOK is enabled. For non-BYOK hosted variants, operators may see masked or redacted request snippets; we document masking policy in the playbook.

4) Subprocessors / cross-border: We maintain a subprocessor list; any subprocessors that process logs are listed and can be scoped out in the DPA. For private VPC/on-prem deployments, we can limit subprocessors to onshore support-only personnel if requested (procurement impact: slightly longer lead time).

Planned next steps: 
- I'll share a short DPA clause draft and operator demarcation language by EOD tomorrow.
- If you want escrow, let's surface exact approval steps in a call with legal procurement.
- We can also provision a restricted-support runbook for your SREs to perform common ops tasks without Redwood operator intervention.

Looping in Irene (security) and Karthik (legal-tech) to add detail and DPA language.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Product Security (Redwood Inference)

Attachments: redwood-private-deploy-keystore-playbook_v1.docx (playbook, 7 pages)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Adding a few technical guardrails we typically include in the DPA/SOW: 

- Telemetry scoping: Operators are limited to non-content telemetry (request id, RPC timings, aggregate token counts, error traces but not plaintext). If a customer requests deeper traces for debugging, we run a controlled session where data is either redacted client-side or keys are temporarily authorized by the customer via a signed approval.

- Key lifecycle: We require explicit customer confirmation for key rotation windows and for key escrow retrieval. Escrow retrieval will be logged to the customer's audit log and requires two-person approval (customer ops + Redwood security).

- Retention/evidence: We can provide on-demand SOC2 sample artifacts and selective logs; production retention windows are configurable by contract.

- Minimal operator footprint: For private deploys we can ship an ops-agent image that exposes a limited troubleshooting API your on-call can run; that reduces the need for Redwood staff access.

I've attached an anonymized operator log sample to show what metadata looks like.

—Irene
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Susan — confirmed: with BYOK and no escrow Redwood operators have no ability to decrypt customer prompts or responses. We'll provide an explicit DPA paragraph to that effect.

Draft clauses I'm proposing (short):
- \"Key Custody\": Customer retains exclusive control of cryptographic keys. Redwood shall not export, store, or have access to customer master keys when BYOK is selected, except as explicitly set out in an escrow addendum.
- \"Operator Access\": Redwood personnel shall only have access to non-content metadata required for service support. Any support session that requires access to plaintext content must be initiated by the customer and logged; access requires customer authorization and two-person Redwood approval.
- \"Escrow Conditions\": Escrow retrieval is permitted only upon (a) customer written approval; (b) documented emergency incident; and (c) signed retrieval form executed by customer security and Redwood security. Retrieval events are auditable and reversible actions are recorded.

I'll attach the text file with suggested DPA snippets and our current subprocessor list for your review. If the language looks ok to you, Tessa/Irène and I can join procurement/legal on a 30 min call tomorrow morning.

Next steps:
